description: Sayadieh is a classic Middle Eastern seafood dish that combines fragrant rice with tender fish and deeply caramelized onions. This comforting meal is infused with warming spices, creating a symphony of flavors and textures that transports you straight to the shores of the Levant. It is a true celebration of the sea, perfect for any family gathering or special occasion.

instructions.title: Prepare and Fry the Fish
instructions.text: Season the fish fillets generously with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of the Sayadieh spice blend. Lightly dredge each fillet in all-purpose flour, shaking off any excess. Heat a generous amount of olive oil in a large, deep pot or pan over medium-high heat. Fry the fish until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Remove the cooked fish and set aside on a plate.

instructions.title: Caramelize the Onions
instructions.text: In the same pot with the remaining oil (add a little more if needed), add the thinly sliced yellow onions. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes until the onions are deeply caramelized and dark brown. This deep color is crucial for the traditional Sayadieh rice. Once caramelized, remove about half of the onions and set them aside to use as a garnish later.

instructions.title: Build the Rice Base
instructions.text: To the remaining caramelized onions in the pot, add the rest of the Sayadieh spice blend. Stir and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, allowing the spices to bloom. Add the rinsed and well-drained basmati rice to the pot, stirring gently to coat the grains thoroughly with the onion and spice mixture. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Cook the Fragrant Rice
instructions.text: Pour in the fish stock or water and season with salt to taste. Bring the liquid to a rolling boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to the lowest setting, cover the pot tightly with a lid, and let it simmer undisturbed for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Resist the urge to lift the lid during this cooking time.

instructions.title: Rest and Fluff the Rice
instructions.text: After the rice has finished simmering, remove the pot from the heat but keep it covered. Let the rice rest for an additional 10 minutes. This resting period allows the steam to redistribute and finish cooking the rice, resulting in perfectly fluffy grains. After resting, gently fluff the rice with a fork to separate the grains.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully arrange the previously fried fish fillets on top of the fluffy, aromatic Sayadieh rice. Garnish generously with the reserved deeply caramelized onions and a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side, allowing each diner to squeeze lemon juice over their portion for a burst of freshness.

tips: For the deepest flavor and color in your rice, ensure the onions are caramelized until very dark brown, almost burnt, but not actually burnt. This process extracts the rich, sweet, and slightly bitter notes essential for Sayadieh.

Using homemade fish stock will elevate the taste significantly. If using water, consider adding a fish bouillon cube or a small piece of fish to simmer with the onions briefly before adding rice for extra depth.
Sayadieh is traditionally served with a simple tahini sauce or a fresh Arabic salad. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice over the fish and rice right before eating brightens all the flavors.
